## Notes from the betting table

**One bet, and it is deliberately small.** `pitch-6f2d18` is the whole of cycle 37. The room's
argument was that the backend has never lowered a scan of any kind, so the honest unit of work is
one operator taken all the way down — lowered, run, and benched against the CPU reference — rather
than three operators half-lowered. Two weeks of appetite against three people at a half, a quarter
and a whole is not much capacity, and that is the point: if one scan cannot be finished inside it,
the estimate for the rest of the operator set is wrong and we would rather find that out in
September than in February.

**Why Chiffchaff is at 0.25.** He is on the port for one day a week and on his own thesis for the
other four. Writing 1.0 here and then explaining the slip afterwards is how the last two cycles
went over; the number in the record is the number the room agreed to.

**Redpoll holds two things at once, and that is not an accident.** The lowering and the benchmark
are both `in_progress` under him. The benchmark is mostly waiting on machine time, so it was left
running alongside rather than queued behind. The plan shows both spans overlapping, which is
what was decided, not a scheduling mistake.

**Left out: the year-end hardening.** Whimbrel wanted the API freeze in this cycle. It was pushed
to 38 because freezing an interface that has lowered exactly one operator would freeze the wrong
interface. It goes in the next bet, standing behind this one.

*The availability figures above are invented, like everything else in this corpus. They are typed
to be different from each other and from the nominal 1.0, because a single global rate cannot show
whether the scheduler divides a size by the people who are actually on it.*
